chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from Ali ibn Ibrahim from his father from Hammad ibn Isa from Hariz from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the saying of Allah, Exalted and Mighty: 'And remember Allah during numbered days.' He said: 'The Takbir (saying Allahu Akbar) is during the Days of Tashriq for the Dhuhr prayer from the Day of Sacrifice until the Fajr prayer on the third day, and in the cities (AmSar) there are ten prayers. When the people depart after the first one, the people of the cities and whoever stays in Mina and prays Dhuhr and Asr there should cease (the continuous Takbir).'
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling and timing for reciting Takbir during the Days of Tashriq after Eid al-Adha?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Tusi records this narration from the chain of Hammad ibn Isa to clarify the specific timing of the Takbir al-Taqbir, distinguishing between the extended recitation in Mina until Fajr of the 13th and the ten prayers in other cities. This ruling highlights the jurisprudential nuance in Shia fiqh regarding the cessation of public glorification after the pilgrims depart, emphasizing the communal aspect of the ritual in different geographical contexts.
